rows.statement: Tesla positions FSD as heading toward full autonomy

sides.text: As our technology continues to advance, we get closer to making a fully autonomous future possible.
Tesla changes meaning of 'Full Self-Driving', gives up on promise of autonomy

rows.statement: Unsupervised FSD will unlock robotaxis and Cybercab

sides.text: With Full Self-Driving (Unsupervised), autonomous driving will be made possible, unlocking our fleet of robotaxis and making Cybercab a reality.

Since 2013, Tesla CEO Elon Musk has repeatedly predicted that the company would achieve fully autonomous driving (SAE Level 5) within one to three years, but as of July 2026, these goals are still to be met.

rows.statement: FSD drives almost anywhere with minimal intervention

sides.text: When enabled, your vehicle will drive you almost anywhere with your active supervision, requiring minimal intervention.
Tesla Full Self Driving requires human intervention every 13 miles

rows.statement: FSD is 7x safer than a human driver

sides.text:
7x

Than a Human Driver When FSD (Supervised) Is Engaged
Critics argue that Tesla has published misleading safety claims about its Autopilot driver-assistance system, and that Tesla cars are actually less safe with Autopilot activated.

rows.statement: Tesla performed the world's first autonomous car delivery

sides.text: Watch the World's First Autonomous Car Delivery

rows.statement: FSD trained on over 100 years of scenarios from over six million vehicles

sides.text: Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is trained on what amounts to over 100 years of anonymous real-world driving scenarios from our fleet of over six million vehicles.

rows.statement: Currently enabled FSD features are not autonomous and need driver supervision

sides.text: Currently enabled features require active driver supervision and do not make the vehicle autonomous.

Tesla Autopilot/FSD is an advanced driver-assistance system (ADAS) developed by Tesla, Inc. that provides partial vehicle automation, corresponding to Level 2 automation as defined by SAE International.

rows.statement: Currently enabled FSD features are not autonomous and need driver supervision

sides.text: Currently enabled features require active driver supervision and do not make the vehicle autonomous.
At no point can a Level 2 system, also known as partial driving automation, ever replace the driver.

rows.statement: FSD (Supervised) available in North America, Europe and Asia Pacific markets

sides.text: Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is currently available in select markets across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific with expansion to additional regions expected with future updates.
Following a roadmap released by the Tesla AI team in late 2024,[170] FSD (Supervised) began rolling out to major international markets throughout 2025 and 2026.

rows.statement: FSD includes automatic parking and summoning the car to you

sides.text: Your Tesla vehicle will automatically detect and maneuver into perpendicular and parallel parking spots for you.

As of February 2026, customers can subscribe to an optional Level 2 package called "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)" (FSD), which adds semi-autonomous navigation on nearly all roads, self-parking, and the ability to summon the car from a parking space.

rows.statement: FSD is sold as a monthly subscription
